name: Agentic Architecture Sandbox (Azure AI Foundry + Claude)
tag: Design a multi-step agent system on Azure AI Foundry with Claude and see cost and speed before you build it.

scenarios.title: Claims intake pipeline
scenarios.ask: Design an insurance claims intake flow with {agents} agents handling {claims} claims a day, using {model} for the reasoning step.
steps: Canvas
Laid out {agents} agents: the core four (Intake, Document reader, Policy checker, Router) plus {=agents - 4} specialists for fraud and medical bills.
Foundry mapping
Mapped each agent to an Azure AI Foundry agent with its own tools and a shared thread store.
Simulator
Ran {=min(500, claims)} synthetic claims through the flow. Median time {=round(3 + agents * 1.5 + model * 0.5, 1)} seconds per claim.
Cost model
Estimated model and hosting cost per claim at about ${=round(0.002 * agents + 0.006 * model, 3)}.
Reviewer
Flagged that the Router has no fallback if the Policy checker times out.
followups: Why not use the top model everywhere?
Most steps are reading and routing, where a smaller model does the job. Keeping the top tier for the reasoning step usually gives most of the quality for a fraction of the cost.
Is this deployed to our Azure tenant?
Not in the sandbox. When you are ready, it exports templates you can deploy into your own subscription after your team reviews them.

scenarios.title: Compare two agent patterns
scenarios.ask: Should our contract-review system use one supervisor with workers or a fixed pipeline? We review {contracts} contracts a week.
steps: Canvas
Built both designs side by side: Supervisor with 3 workers, and a 4-stage pipeline.
Simulator
Ran 50 sample contracts of about {pages} pages through each.
Analyzer
Supervisor caught {=min(9, 3 + round(pages / 15))} more unusual clauses per 100 contracts. The pipeline was {=round(20 + pages / 4)}% cheaper.
Advisor
Suggested the pipeline for standard contracts and the supervisor only for contracts flagged as unusual.

result.title: Pattern comparison
rows: Hybrid: pipeline first, supervisor for flagged ones

followups: How many contracts would go to the supervisor?
In the simulation about 15% were flagged, so roughly {=round(contracts * 0.15)} a week at your volume.
Yes. Every clause finding links to the passage and the step that raised it.

scenarios.title: Plan for a traffic spike
scenarios.ask: Our support agents normally handle {base} requests an hour. What happens at {spike}x during a launch?
steps: Simulator
Replayed {=base * spike} requests an hour through the current design.
Bottleneck finder
The retrieval step saturates first at about {=round(base * 2.5)} requests an hour.
Advisor
Suggested a response cache and a queue with a friendly wait message above the limit.
Re-run
With changes, the flow held {=base * spike} requests an hour with no dropped requests in the simulation.
followups: Will real traffic behave like the simulation?
Not exactly. The sandbox uses your traffic shape from the last month, but a real launch can differ. Plan a load test before the date.
What does the wait message say?
You write it. A common choice is an honest estimate of wait time and an option to get an email reply instead.
